summary.text: 本 points to the root or base of a tree. It takes 木, “tree,” and adds a short horizontal mark near the bottom to highlight the roots. This gives the abstract senses “origin,” “source,” and “basis” a concrete image: the part from which the tree grows.

history.text: The Shuowen describes the bottom of the tree as 本 and notes the added line underneath. The extra stroke acts as a pointer within the tree picture; its position tells the reader which part to attend to.
